caveats: Counts are salmon gene-level output as delivered and may be non-integer; the QC must not assume integer counts
With 4 replicates per group, a single departing sample is not re-analyzed here — flag it for the report step
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-multi-group-3x4-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples; gene identifier in the first column; salmon gene-level counts as delivered) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-multi-group-3x4-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (one row per sample: sample, condition in {control, treated_a, treated_b}). Build a DESeqDataSet from the counts as delivered (no scaling, no log) with the condition column. Apply the variance-stabilizing transformation blind to the design, run PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a heatmap of Euclidean distances between samples; color both by condition. Single batch, so no batch coloring. Report per-sample library sizes.

steps.description: Blind-vst PCA and sample-distance structure check of the 12 samples, colored by condition, with library sizes reported.
acceptance_criteria: PCA and distance heatmap produced and saved, colored by condition (control, treated_a, treated_b)
A statement on whether samples cluster by condition and whether any sample departs from its group

steps.name: DESeq2 omnibus LRT + per-treatment vs-control Wald contrasts
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred: salmon gene-level table as delivered, no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table — fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression
Do not run tximport on a gene table (tximport imports transcript estimates) and do not invent a length input
The LRT answers the any-difference question; a Wald test on one coefficient does not, because condition spans two coefficients
The FDR holds within each contrast, not across contrasts — label every table with its contrast
With 4 replicates per group, DESeq2 sets p-values to NA rather than replacing counts for flagged outliers — expect some NA p-values and report their count
steps.context: 1. Read counts.csv and metadata.csv; merge on sample name; set condition as a factor with explicit reference level control (relevel before the model; do not rely on alphabetical order). 2. Pre-filter: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (smallest group size); report genes kept and dropped. 3. Fit DESeq with design ~ condition; do not pre-normalize or transform the counts — the median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model. 4. Import state: this is a salmon gene-level table as delivered, with no per-sample quantification files (quant.sf / abundance.h5) and no average transcript length table. Fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset; do not run tximport on a gene table; do not invent a length input; record in the output that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. 5. Any-difference question: likelihood ratio test, full model ~ condition vs reduced model ~ 1 (no nuisance terms exist to keep). 6. Per-treatment questions: named Wald contrasts c("condition","treated_a","control") and c("condition","treated_b","control") (factor, numerator, denominator). 7. With 4 replicates per group (<7), DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets the p-value and padj of those genes to NA: keep this behavior on; report the number of genes with NA p-values from the outlier flag separately from genes removed by the independent filter; inspect the counts of any flagged gene of interest. 8. Shrink the log2FC of both contrasts with ashr (lfcShrink, type = "ashr", contrast = ...); p-values come from the unshrunken fit; keep the unshrunken estimate beside the shrunken one. 9. Multiple testing: BH adjustment within each of the three tables (LRT table, treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) at alpha = 0.05 with independent filtering on (pass alpha = 0.05 to results); select genes by padj < 0.05; label each table with its contrast. 10. Inspect a histogram of unadjusted p-values for each table before trusting the adjusted values; report the shape (flat or left-peak expected). 11. If row identifiers are not HGNC symbols, map them to gene symbols (via the EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86 annotation, or the provisioned human gene identifier mapping: UniProt human ID mapping, headerless, Entrez GeneID / RefSeq / Ensembl columns, multi-valued cells '; '-separated); add a symbol column to all tables and report the mapping rate. 12. Set a random seed at script start and record it in the outputs. Save: the three results tables (CSV), the DESeqDataSet (rds), MA plot and dispersion plot per contrast and for the omnibus, and the p-value histograms.
steps.question: Of the 12,000 genes, which differ across the three groups (control, treated_a, treated_b) at all, and which genes does treated_a, and which does treated_b, each change relative to control?

steps.name: Report with edgeR robustness overlap
caveats: Do not present the union of the two methods' gene sets as the result — the intersection is the high-confidence set, and method-specific genes are a secondary set
The FDR is controlled per contrast; do not pool contrasts into a single adjusted p-value without stating that choice
steps.context: 1. Robustness (second method): on the same pre-filtered count matrix and the same design (~ condition, reference control), run the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test: glmQLFit; a QL F-test on the set of condition coefficients as the omnibus any-difference test; per-contrast QL tests for treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control. Report the number of significant genes (padj < 0.05) from DESeq2 and from edgeR for each question, and the size of the intersection. Treat the intersection as the high-confidence set; list genes called by only one method as a secondary set with that method's name; do not present the union as the result. 2. Report content: method (DESeq2 LRT + Wald contrasts; edgeR QL F-test as second method), package versions, the design formula ~ condition, the explicit reference level control, each named contrast, the thresholds (padj < 0.05; no fold-change threshold — the question asks for no effect-size threshold), number of genes tested after the pre-filter, number of DE genes per contrast, sessionInfo, and the random seed. 3. Gene tables: rank genes by the shrunken log2FC (name the shrinkage estimator, ashr, in the table header); show log2FoldChange (unshrunken, from the test), shrunken_log2FoldChange, and lfcSE for each gene; p-values from the unshrunken fit; label every table with its contrast; include the gene symbol column. 4. Diagnostics before the gene tables: MA plot and dispersion plot (state what each shows) and the p-value histograms (state their shape). 5. Required statements: the length offset is lost (salmon gene-level counts as delivered, no length input; a change in isoform use can show as differential expression); the count of genes with NA p-values from the outlier flag; that the FDR holds per contrast, not across contrasts.
steps.question: What is the final reproducible report: which genes differ across the three groups at all, which genes each treatment changes relative to control, and how robust are those sets to a second method (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test)?
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
steps.description: Runs the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method on the same design, reports the overlap, and assembles the final report with diagnostics, per-contrast gene tables, and the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Final report names the method, package versions, design formula, reference level control, each contrast, thresholds, number of genes tested, and number of DE genes per contrast
sessionInfo and the random seed are present in the report

For each question, the significant-gene counts from DESeq2 and edgeR and the size of their intersection are reported; the intersection is labeled the high-confidence set; method-specific genes are listed as a secondary set named by method
MA and dispersion plots and p-value histograms are present before the gene tables, each with a statement of what it shows
Gene tables are ranked by shrunken log2FC and carry log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, and lfcSE columns, each table labeled with its contrast
The statement that the length offset is lost is present in the report

plan.title: Liver two-treatment DE: omnibus LRT + vs-control contrasts
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are 12,000 genes x 12 samples of salmon gene-level counts as delivered (length correction unknown) from human liver: 3 conditions (control, treated_a, treated_b), 4 unpaired replicates each, single batch, no covariates. The research question has two parts — genes that differ across the three groups at all, and genes each treatment changes relative to control — which maps onto the DESeq2 multi-group procedure: first sample-structure QC (blind vst, PCA, distance heatmap) so that samples are seen to cluster by condition before any test; then a DESeq2 model on the counts as delivered (no length offset, because only a gene-level salmon table is available — no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table; the lost offset is stated in the plan and report), with explicit reference level control, a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples) and median-of-ratios normalization inside the model. The any-difference question is answered by a likelihood ratio test (full ~ condition vs reduced ~ 1); the per-treatment questions by named Wald contrasts treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control, with ashr shrinkage of the contrast fold changes and BH adjustment within each contrast at alpha 0.05. A final report step runs the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as the second method, reports the overlap (intersection = high-confidence set), and assembles diagnostics (MA/dispersion plots, p-value histograms), per-contrast gene tables ranked by shrunken log2FC, and the reproducibility record.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA on top variable genes + sample distance heatmap
DESeq2 pre-filter: >= 10 counts in >= smallest group size samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the negative binomial model, no pre-normalization
DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ condition, explicit reference level control, gene counts without length offset
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (full ~ condition vs reduced ~ 1) then pairwise Wald contrasts each level vs reference
ashr log2 fold change shrinkage for the contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, independent filtering, alpha 0.05
report with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as second method, overlap as high-confidence set

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA on top variable genes + sample distance heatmap
DESeq2 pre-filter: >= 10 counts in >= smallest group size samples
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the negative binomial model, no pre-normalization
DESeq2 fixed-effects design ~ condition, explicit reference level control, gene counts without length offset
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (full ~ condition vs reduced ~ 1) then pairwise Wald contrasts each level vs reference
ashr log2 fold change shrinkage for the contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, independent filtering, alpha 0.05
report with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as second method, overlap as high-confidence set
